paragraphs: AppsAnywhere sells a cloud-based platform that higher education institutions use to deliver applications at scale to lab devices and student-owned devices alike. It combines physical and virtual workloads to deliver apps on and off campus through one centralized platform for students, staff, and faculty.

Administrators configure access by context, including user groups, device type, operating system, hardware profiles, and location. The platform then picks a delivery route for each launch based on factors such as device type, operating system, geographical location, and whether the machine is user-owned or university-managed. Real-time app metering shows which titles are underused or not used at all. A managed Cloud Delivery service streams Windows applications to any device directly in a browser, with sessions running in a clean, non-persistent environment that resets each time.

Institutions start with a catalog of over 150 pre-packaged higher education applications that are updated frequently. The company says it supports integrations with existing delivery technologies so customers need not rip and replace current infrastructure. It states compliance with WCAG 2.2 AA standards, full keyboard and speech navigation, and significant screen-reader functionality. Product translations ship out of the box in languages including Catalan, Norwegian, and Welsh.

quote.text: One centralized software portal for students and faculty on any device.
